questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Botswana?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter G and has 8 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Botswana article.

questions.proof: The capital of Botswana is Gaborone.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Botswana?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter N and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Botswana article.

questions.proof: The countries that border Botswana are Zimbabwe, South Africa, and Namibia.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Botswana?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter E and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Botswana article.

questions.proof: Botswana has two official languages: Setswana and English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is also possible to travel from Botswana directly into _____ by crossing the Zambezi River by ferry.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter Z and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Botswana article.

questions.proof: It is also possible to travel from Botswana directly into Zambia by crossing the Zambezi River by ferry.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The economy of Botswana has been growing very fast since it became an independent country in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the 60s of the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Botswana article.

questions.proof: The economy of Botswana has been growing very fast since it became an independent country in 1966.
